summary: Anton Westermann was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig from 1825 to 1830 and served there as Mitdirektor from 1830 to 1865.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Anton Zigmund-Cerbu studied at the University of Bucharest, EPHE, and INALCO, completing his doctorate under Jean Filliozat and Rolf Alfred Stein in 1952. He held posts at the CNRS (1952) and Columbia University (1960).

Antonello Palumbo is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He held posts as a researcher at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2004) and at SOAS University of London (attested 2005–2010).

Antoni Józef Śmieszek worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from Jagiellonian University and studied at Munich, Berlin, and London. He served as Assistant Professor at Adam Mickiewicz University (1922–1935) and Professor of Egyptology at the University of Warsaw (1934–1939).

Antoni Kałuski was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Jagiellonian University from 1912 to 1915 under Jan Michał Rozwadowski and Andrzej Gawroński, and later studied at the University of Chicago.

Antoni Muchliński was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the Imperial University of Vilna (1824–1828) and served on the faculty at Saint Petersburg State University from around 1835 to 1866.

Antonia Ruppel works in Indology and linguistics. She held posts at Cornell University (attested 2014–2015), Oxford (attested 2019–2022), Halle-Wittenberg (attested 2022), the University of Munich (attested 2021–2023, 2025), and the University of New Mexico (attested 2026).

Antonie Rutgers was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Groningen and Leiden University under Hendrik Arent Hamaker. From 1837 to 1875, he served as extraordinary Professor of Hebrew at Leiden University.

Antonino Forte worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held professorial posts at Hōbōgirin (around 1976–1986), the Italian School of East Asian Studies (around 1982–2000), and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (around 1988–2006).

Antonino Pagliaro specialized in Iranian/Central Asian studies, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Palermo, Florence, Heidelberg (under Christian Bartholomae), and Vienna (under Paul Kretschmer), later serving as Professor of Glottology at Sapienza University of Rome (1936–1968).

Antonio Agostino Giorgi was a scholar in Tibetology and Indology who studied under Giovanni Lorenzo Berti. He served as Professor of sacred writings at Sapienza University of Rome from 1746 and as librarian at the Biblioteca Angelica from 1752.
Antonio Faiani was an Indology scholar. During his career, he served as Director of Liceo Classico Massimo d'Azeglio and Director of Liceo Ariosto.
Antonio Marazzi was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia.

Antonio Rigopoulos is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara (1987–1994) and was appointed Full Professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice in 1999.

Antonio T. de Nicolás worked in philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD from Fordham University and served as professor emeritus of philosophy at Stony Brook University, where he held a post from around 1968 to 2022.

Antonio Terrone is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, and has served as scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Antonio Vigilante specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning his doctorate at the University of Bari (2009–2012), his posts include teaching at Liceo Enea Silvio Piccolomini (2015), Educazione Aperta (2023), and the University of Siena (2025–2026).

Antonín Jan Jungmann was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied medicine at Charles University (1800–1805). He subsequently served as Professor of Medicine at Charles University from 1808 to 1850.

Anuj Misra works in history/archaeology and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Canterbury under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker, later holding posts at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science and Free University of Berlin in 2024.

Anukul Chandra Banerjee worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at the University of Calcutta under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and Nalinaksha Dutt, he served as department head at Calcutta and as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1981–1982).
